summary:
First testing pass on PPE Pro Solutions e-commerce app. Backend API: 22/22 tests passing (100%). Frontend: All pages load (home, /products, industry pages, material pages, product detail, /quote, /contact, /about, /sizing-guide, /glove-guide, all 5 policy pages), navbar Industries dropdown opens with all 6 items, filters work (20 → 3 products when Chloroprene selected), quote form submits successfully with toast + success card, product detail shows size/pack/quantity selectors, add-to-cart populates the cart drawer with correct item. NO console errors observed across the entire site.

CRITICAL BUG DISCOVERED: Cart persistence is broken. localStorage is being overwritten to `[]` on every page navigation due to a useEffect race condition in CartContext.jsx. This breaks the entire Cart → Checkout → Order flow — users cannot check out because /cart and /checkout always show 'empty cart' after leaving the product page.

ui_bugs.issue: Cart never persists across navigation. Add-to-Cart correctly writes to localStorage (verified: `ppe_cart_v1` has the item), but on the NEXT page load, the write-effect (line 21-23) fires BEFORE the read-effect (line 12-19) populates state — resulting in `[]` being written to localStorage, clobbering the stored cart. Confirmed via evaluate(localStorage.getItem(...)) which returns `[]` on /cart and /checkout even when seeded beforehand. Consequence: /cart page shows 'Your cart is empty' and /checkout redirects to empty state, so the entire checkout flow cannot be exercised.

integration_issues.issue: Blocked by the localStorage race condition above. Because the cart empties on navigation, POST /api/orders never fires from the UI (backend endpoint itself works correctly — verified via pytest, including out-of-stock 400, case pricing math, expedited/pickup shipping cost logic).

action_items: After the fix, re-verify the full checkout flow: Add to Cart → /cart shows item → /checkout renders shipping form → submit creates order → /order-confirmation/:orderNumber shows the PPE-XXXXXX number and line items.
critical_code_review_comments: CartContext.jsx has a classic React useEffect ordering bug: two independent effects (one reads localStorage → setItems, one writes items → localStorage) both fire after first mount. On first mount `items` is [], the write effect fires with that value, overwriting whatever the user had stored, before the read effect's setItems takes effect. Use a lazy initializer.

server.py generate_order_number() uses random digits with no uniqueness check — extremely unlikely collision in demo data, but for production would need to guard against duplicate order_numbers or use ObjectId/UUID.

server.py CORS middleware is added AFTER app.include_router(api_router). In Starlette/FastAPI this still works because middlewares wrap the whole ASGI app, but conventionally add_middleware should be called before include_router for clarity.

seed_data.py has one stray `industries_note` field on gloveworks-blue-nitrile-industrial-6mil (line 374) that isn't part of the Product model — currently silently dropped by pydantic (extra='ignore' via BaseDocument). Not a bug, but dead data.
No pagination on GET /api/products — fine for 20 seeded items, would need it for real catalog scale.

success_rate.frontend: ~85% — all pages render, all forms except checkout submit correctly, but the cart persistence bug blocks the entire checkout path (~15% of critical flow)

test_credentials: N/A — no auth on this site
seed_data_creation: None — used the 20 products auto-seeded on backend startup. Test data created via API in pytest is prefixed with 'TEST' in email/name fields (quotes, contacts, orders) — no explicit cleanup, but this is a demo/preview environment.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is fully validated and stable — pytest at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py covers all endpoints including order pricing math (box vs case tier), shipping cost tiers (standard $12, expedited +$35, pickup $0, free over $150), out-of-stock 400s, and product/order 404s. Only re-run backend if server.py changes. Frontend: only one bug (CartContext.jsx race condition) blocks the checkout flow — after main agent applies the lazy-init fix, verify end-to-end: add product → /cart shows item → /checkout form renders → fill shipping (fields likely use data-testid, not name=; inspect via `page.query_selector_all('form input')` on /checkout) → submit → order confirmation page shows PPE-XXXXXX order number. Everything else (home, industry filtering, material pages, quote form, contact form, all policy pages, navbar dropdowns) was verified working in this iteration with zero console errors.
rca of the issue:
CartContext.jsx CartProvider declares useState with initial value `[]`, then two useEffects:
  1) useEffect(read localStorage, [])
  2) useEffect(write items to localStorage, [items])

On first mount, React runs both effects in declaration order after paint. Effect #1 calls setItems(stored) — this SCHEDULES a state update, but does not immediately mutate `items` for effect #2. Effect #2 then runs with items still equal to [] (the initial state that was rendered), and writes `[]` to localStorage — clobbering the stored cart. Later, the queued setItems triggers a re-render; effect #2 fires again and writes the (now correct in-memory) items back to storage. HOWEVER, on any subsequent full page load (navigation), the localStorage was already clobbered by the previous session's mount cycle if the user hadn't modified the cart on that page. In practice: user adds item on product page → localStorage populated → user clicks /cart link → new full mount → items=[] → effect#2 writes [] to storage → effect#1 reads [] (now stale) → items stays [] → user sees empty cart forever.

Reproduction:
  1. Open /products/skintx-black-nitrile-5mil
  2. Click 'Add to Cart' — drawer opens with item, localStorage has cart JSON
  3. Press Escape, then navigate to /cart (or /checkout, or refresh)
  4. Observe: cart shows 'Your cart is empty', localStorage ppe_cart_v1 is '[]'

Mitigation: Use lazy useState initializer as described in action_items — this reads localStorage synchronously during render initialization, so `items` is populated before the first render commits, and effect #2 always writes the correct value.
